result:
I found 10 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behaviour didn't match their docstrings, and fixed all of them. I then checked all 150 rules against the docstrings with a script over many quantity/unit-price combinations, and every rule now matches.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 25, 77, 117 | The cap was applied to the amount being discounted instead of to the discount | The discount is calculated first, then capped |
| 45 | The cap only kicked in when the discount was over 200,000 won | The cap always applies |
| 49, 89, 147 | Discounts were rounded with `round()` instead of floored | Changed to floor (`//`) |
| 76 | Threshold was 51 units instead of 50 | Changed to `qty >= 50` |
| 92, 134 | `>` was used, so exactly 20 (rule 92) or 30 (rule 134) units got no discount | Changed to `>=` |

I also changed two more comparisons so they read the same as the docstring: rule 28 (`> 10` to `>= 10`) and rule 57 (`>= 13` to `>= 12`). Neither changes any price, because a "marginal" rule gives a 0-won discount at exactly the threshold quantity anyway.

STATUS: DONE
